verdict: Yes. With only what this run surfaced, a wallet-holding agent has the store, product, price (0.05), mint and token program (R8), a validated order (R9 order_valid true), the signer sequence (R9 signers[0].sequence), the full prepare_purchase payload shape (R3), and the verify/submit argument names (R3 + R7). It stops exactly where it should: the buyer address must come from a human-enrolled signer (PayBox OAuth, Phantom local, Privy login), and this run held no signer.
single_most_valuable_change: Move the headless signer path (PayBox SDK / Privy CLI) and one exact, schema-matching argument list for verify_signed_transaction and submit_transaction into agents.md, so the runbook alone, not the refusal, carries a headless agent from menu to submit.
